findings.one_line: The cited record establishes Algorithm 2's M_AOG/M_DOG output, but not the lemma's added Algorithm-1 partition/order and exhaustive legal-reconstruction assertions; those assertions are then load-bearing for the image domain.

The attested Proposition 2 is conditioned on 'conventional faithfulness', whereas this lemma substitutes rank faithfulness without a derivation that the latter supplies the cited hypothesis; the plateau minimality proof relies on that substitution.

The proposed two-row witness never derives its recovered AOG sets R_1={u,v}, K_1=C_src or proves all 2q choices are Algorithm-2 legal; generic avoidance and the cited recovery theorem do not establish these instance-specific witness memberships.

The proof asserts, without a declared bridge, that the Yang minimum-DOG class on the no-measurement subclass is exactly the full unknown-graph canonical lvLiNGAM class quantified by Tramontano et al.; normalized-column algebra alone does not give this iff.

For arbitrary promised rational inputs the proof invokes deterministic joint-image attainment, but that theorem is not a dependency; its listed complete-image theorem is generic-population only and cannot supply the rational conclusion.
No proved statement consumes the external coverage premise, so deleting it broadens no headline result in this population core.

cited_checks.note: The supplied attestation states Algorithm 2 outputs M_AOG and M_DOG under Assumptions 3 and 4 (and identification up to DOG under 1,3,4); it does not state the added Algorithm-1 partition-in-causal-order or exhaustive legal-reconstruction clauses.
The attested Proposition 2 conclusion is under 'conventional faithfulness'; the core claim applies it under LV-SEM-ME rank faithfulness, with no supplied equivalence of those hypotheses.
With j=u and i=v, the attested Theorem 3.3 has the same observed-descendant equality and the same deletion of arrows into u.

The supplied Appendix A.4.1 attestation gives the invertible rewrite and probability-zero preservation; the attested finite-class argument yields simultaneous faithfulness by a finite union of null exceptional sets.
